sections.title: Meeting Someone New
sections.content: When you bring two friends together, the verb is 'presentar': 'Te presento a Daniela' — this is Daniela, literally 'I introduce Daniela to you'. The other person answers 'mucho gusto', which you already know, and whoever is hosting says 'bienvenido' to a man and 'bienvenida' to a woman.

sections.title: Why, and because
sections.content: '¿Por qué?' is two words with an accent, and it asks the question. 'Porque' is one word with no accent, and it gives the answer. They sound almost the same out loud, so the spelling is what tells them apart.

items.spanish: Carlos, quiero presentarte a mis amigos.
items.english: Carlos, I want to introduce you to my friends.

items.spanish: Te presento a mi amiga Daniela.

items.english: Nice to meet you, Carlos. Welcome.

items.spanish: ¿Por qué estudias español? Porque quiero viajar y hablar con muchas personas.
items.english: Why do you study Spanish? Because I want to travel and talk to lots of people.

sections.content: 'Presentar' needs an 'a' before the person: 'Te presento a Daniela', never 'Te presento Daniela'.
